source_snapshot.title: test(upgrade): cover an IX_HOME containing a space
source_snapshot.body:
Closes the one open question from the #391/#392 review. Everything else Joey raised is fixed and merged — I verified the two blocking ones independently before writing this:

- the stamp is now `0.9.4+release.<sha>`, and running it through `main`'s own `splitVersion`/`isNewer` gives `[0,9,4]`, `[1,0,0]`, `[2,3,1]` with **no downgrade at any version**;
- `recover()` now tests `existsSync(join(dest, intact))` rather than the bare directory, so a `.version`-only husk no longer counts as present and the backup survives.

## The question this covers

#349's reporter is on `[local-path] 10`, and their confirmed workaround was pointing TEMP at a space-free path.

#392 moved the upgrade scratch from `[local-path] — an 8.3 alias, which **never contains a space** — to `[local-path] 10\.ix\...`, which does. If that failure is space-driven rather than short-path-driven, the move put a space onto the upgrade path where there previously wasn't one.

## What this can and cannot do

It **cannot settle the mechanism.** It runs on whatever platform CI is on, and the suspected fault is a Windows path provider.

What it does is prove our own code carries no space-free assumption — so when the reporter tries again, the remaining suspects are outside this repo. Nothing else in the suite passed a path with a space.

Four cases: preparing a download directory inside a spaced `IX_HOME`, creating one a manual install never made, sweeping orphans out of it, and restoring an interrupted install into it.

## One thing worth reporting from writing it

The sweep case first used `.cli-download-1-abc` and **failed** — pid 1 is init, always alive, so the sweep correctly skipped the directory as an in-flight download owned by another process. That is `isLiveScratch` doing exactly its job, on the first real attempt to trip it. The test now uses a pid that is not running.

759 tests green · tsc clean · lint unchanged (0 errors, 38 pre-existing warnings).
